items.note: Quota page: 500 distributions per AWS account, adjustable (hypothesis 200 is outdated). Looked in cloudfront-limits table 1 and the FAQ (the FAQ points to the quotas page).
Quota page: 75 cache behaviors, 100 origins, 10 origin groups per distribution, all adjustable. Hypothesis (25 / 25 / 10) is outdated except origin groups.

Two statements disagree: quotas page says maximum cacheable file size per HTTP GET response is 50 GB (request body 64 GB); the FAQ (older text) says 30 GB for a single file. Both recorded; adjudicator should keep both with scope or prefer the quotas page.
150 Gbps and 250,000 requests per second per distribution, adjustable, not applied to flat-rate plans. FAQ: request higher limits, capacity added within two business days. Hypothesis confirmed.
100 alternate domain names per distribution, adjustable.

Response timeout 1-120 s (default 30), connection attempts 1-3 (default 3), connection timeout 1-10 s (default 10), keep-alive default 5 s confirmed. Keep-alive range is 1-300 s on the quotas page (hypothesis said 1-120). Origin ports: 80, 443, 1024-65535, defaults 80 and 443.

Default TTL 86400 s (one day), Maximum TTL 31536000 s (one year). The saved pages do not state a default Minimum TTL of 0; 0 appears only in managed cache policy settings (using-managed-cache-policies), not as a default. The max-age and s-maxage interplay is in the table of Expiration (mined by the behavior lens).

First 1,000 paths a month free and wildcard counts as one path confirmed. In-progress limits (3,000 objects, 15 wildcard paths) are only in the FAQ; the current quotas page lists 150 paths or tags per second and 1 wildcard invalidation per second instead. Both recorded. Price after the free paths: $0.005 per path.
Default error caching minimum TTL is 10 seconds (georestrictions page; DownloadDistValuesErrorPages states no number).
4 key groups per cache behavior, 5 public keys per key group, 10 key groups per account; all adjustable.
10 KB code (not adjustable), 2 MB memory, 100 functions per account, submillisecond duration.

Current pages: Lambda@Edge timeout 30 s for all four event types, memory 128 MB for viewer events and 10,240 MB for origin events, code 50 MB for both, generated response 40 KB (viewer) and 1 MB (origin). Hypothesis (viewer 5 s, 1 MB package) is outdated.
5 MB per store, key 512 Bytes, value 1 KB.
10 each per cache policy and per origin request policy (all adjustable), 20 custom cache policies per account.
1 certificate per distribution; 2 dedicated-IP SSL certificates per account by default, adjustable, no quota with SNI.
RSA 1024/2048/3072/4096 bits, max 4096; ECDSA 256 and 384; ACM issues RSA up to 2048 bits.
10 fields per profile, 10 fields in a request body, request body 1 MB, field 16 KB, 10 profiles and 10 configurations per account.
21 addresses for allow-listing, 3 for apex domains (the dual-stack counts are in the FAQ facts); requires price class All (Use all edge locations).
Sampling rate: whole number 1 to 100; delivered to Kinesis Data Streams within seconds, best effort.

Destinations and no extra charge for enabling standard logs are in facts of other lenses. NOT FOUND: how quickly standard log files are delivered; AccessLogs, standard-logging and the FAQ give no delivery time for v2 logs.
Price Class All (default), 200, 100 from the pay-as-you-go price class table.

Dimensions and unit prices from the pay-as-you-go page. NOT FOUND in a quotable line: the unit of request pricing (per 10,000 requests appears only in a heading), so the HTTP and HTTPS request prices were rejected by M5 and not stored.
1 TB data transfer out, 10,000,000 requests, 2,000,000 CloudFront Functions invocations a month (FAQ sentence). Mined mainly by another lens.
$0, $15, $200, $1,000 a month per distribution, no overage charges; allowances 1M/10M/125M/500M requests. Volatile.
At least 99.9% monthly uptime; credits 10%, 25%, 100%.
1,000 to 10,000,000 bytes; status 200, 403 or 404; Accept-Encoding with gzip or br; Content-Length required.
20 standard accelerators, 10 listeners, 10 port ranges, 42 endpoint groups per accelerator, 10 endpoints per endpoint group; one endpoint group per Region per listener.

Two static IPv4; dual-stack four (two IPv4, two IPv6); kept while the accelerator exists, even when disabled; lost on delete (fact global-accelerator-dec-static-ips-deleted-with-accelerator by another lens).
Range 0 to 100, default 100 (CreateEndpointGroup API reference).
Range 0 to 255, default 128.

Interval 10 or 30 s (default 30); threshold count default 3 (range 1-10). Source is the CreateEndpointGroup API reference (fetched by this agent); the developer guide pages give no numbers. Options apply to EC2 and Elastic IP endpoints only.
FAQ: unhealthy endpoint detected and taken out of service in less than one minute. Recovery to regular routing about 30 seconds. The DNS comparison is in facts of the decisions lens.
$0.025 per hour per accelerator, enabled or disabled; DT-Premium in the dominant direction, on top of EC2 data transfer out; public IPv4 charges.
TCP 340 s, UDP 30 s, not customizable.
VPC subnet endpoints with EC2 instances only; subnet /28 to /17. NOT FOUND: the figure 64,000 destinations appears only inside an FAQ question heading, not in an answer or a quotable sentence.
At most two ranges, most specific prefix /24 (FAQ facts by another lens).

There are two commitments: Multi-AZ accelerators (credit tiers start below 99.99%) and Single-AZ accelerators (credit tiers start below 99.5%). The SLA page states the thresholds in tables, not as one sentence.

GA: 130 Points of Presence in 95 cities across 53 countries (features page). CloudFront: only '750+ global edge locations' in the flat-rate plan table. NOT FOUND: 600+ POPs and 13 regional edge caches; the saved CloudFront features, FAQ and Introduction pages list locations but give no totals.

Canned: expiry only, no start time, no IP range, no reuse; custom: optional start time and IP range, reusable with wildcards. Hash-Algorithm values SHA1 and SHA256, default SHA1 on the current pages; the 2026-04-01 SHA-256 What's New item belongs to the changes lens.
Quota table 12: origin response timeout (idle timeout) for WebSocket is 10 minutes.
